title: CONTROL Resonant Beginner's Guide: Where to Start
excerpt: A spoiler-light preparation guide: choose your platform, catch up on the story, learn combat terminology and understand progression before launch.
introduction: A spoiler-light preparation guide: choose your platform, catch up on the story, learn combat terminology and understand progression before launch.
quickAnswer: Start with platform and storage checks, then learn the difference between the Aberrant, Combat Abilities, Talents and Artifacts. You do not have to finish CONTROL first. This is a preparation guide based on published information, not a claim that we have played the retail game.

Before installing: check the right platform information

steps.title: Separate digital, physical and Mac dates
steps.text: A date attached to one format is not automatically the date for another. The release guide keeps those cases separate.

steps.title: Check the final PC table, not the early FAQ
steps.text: The September PC announcement supersedes the initial specifications. Leave room beyond the listed installation size for updates and other files.

steps.title: Check the exact edition on your storefront
steps.text: Compare the actual bonus list and early-access entitlement on the platform where you intend to play. Regional pricing and store inclusions can differ.

sections.title: How much story do you need?
paragraphs: Remedy positions the sequel as a standalone entry point. If you want to learn the world through play, begin without a full plot recap. If you enjoy continuity, the original game provides Jesse's perspective before Dylan's story.

sections.title: Reach is a traversal unlock, not a Combat Ability
paragraphs: The useful distinction is what the reward changes: Reach is described as a way to move through the world. Do not confuse it with the supernatural Combat Abilities awarded by defeating Resonants.
Remedy says story-gated traversal abilities do not carry into New Game Plus. That is a general system rule, not a published Metro Fault replay schedule.

sections.title: How to prepare without following an invented route

steps.title: Learn movement before chasing damage
steps.text: Use the controls and accessibility guides to identify movement options that suit you. A traversal challenge and a damage check require different preparation.

steps.title: Separate the hazard from the enemy
steps.text: When reviewing the footage, pay attention to the environment before choosing a loadout. A weapon tier list cannot explain the direction a moving hazard takes.

steps.title: Record the actual unlock conditions
steps.text: At launch, check the quest log, prerequisites and reward screen before relying on a community route. A preview may begin with abilities already unlocked.

steps.title: Return to incomplete exploration notes
steps.text: If Reach opens a path you could not previously reach, record its exact location. Do not assume that every locked route uses this same ability.

sections.title: What a complete Metro Fault walkthrough still needs
paragraphs: There is no tested step-by-step launch route on this page yet. The missing information is specific: the starting quest, entrance, checkpoints, collectibles, unlock prerequisites and any differences between the preview and retail build.
bullets: A numbered route with identifiable landmarks and actual screenshots.
Collectible locations separated from required objectives.
A confirmed reward screen and any prerequisite quests.

sections.title: What to watch when learning the fight

subsections.title: Read the arena before the health bar
paragraphs: If floor hazards are what end an attempt, begin by identifying safe movement. Increasing damage is not a substitute for understanding where you can stand. The retail encounter will need its own annotated arena guide.

subsections.title: Test one change at a time
paragraphs: Keep your loadout consistent while learning a telegraph. Then change one ability, Artifact or Assist setting so you can tell what helped. This is a learning method, not a proven best build.

subsections.title: Do not assume fire appearance equals an elemental weakness
paragraphs: A boss's visual design is not a damage-resistance table. Compare actual hits under consistent conditions before calling an element effective.

sections.title: Boss rewards and world progression
paragraphs: Resonant victories award Combat Abilities, but the general reward system is not enough to name this boss's exact drop. Some boss rewards offer choices; NG+ expands ability combinations. Treat a claimed item or ability name as unverified unless the reward screen or an explicit source supports it.

title: CONTROL Resonant Difficulty: Parry & Dodge Explained
excerpt: Does CONTROL Resonant have parries? Understand the director's answer, dodge-focused combat and the difference between difficulty and Assist Mode.
introduction: Does CONTROL Resonant have parries? Understand the director's answer, dodge-focused combat and the difference between difficulty and Assist Mode.
quickAnswer: CONTROL Resonant does not use a parry mechanic, according to director Mikael Kasurinen's interview with GamesRadar+. The design focuses on flowing through groups of enemies. Assist Mode provides separate controls for players who want to change the challenge.
imageAlt: CONTROL Resonant official promotional screenshot; scene illustration

sections.title: Can you parry in CONTROL Resonant?
Why there is no parry
paragraphs: Kasurinen describes encounter design around movement between enemies rather than a prolonged exchange with a single opponent. The absence of a parry is a design choice, not a missing input in the button layout.
Remedy's combat explanation instead connects melee, ability power, Falter and executions. Learning those relationships is more useful than searching for a universal counterattack window.

sections.title: Difficulty and Assist Mode are different questions
paragraphs: Assist Mode lets players adjust particular sources of pressure, including enemy aggression, dodge timing and projectile speed. Remedy says using these options does not prevent trophies or achievements.

links.label: See the complete Assist Mode settings table

sections.title: A practical learning order

steps.title: Identify what interrupted your attack
steps.text: Was the problem an enemy telegraph, camera position, a floor hazard or an empty resource meter? Name the problem before changing every setting.

steps.title: Practice movement with a familiar weapon
steps.text: A consistent moveset makes it easier to distinguish timing mistakes from unfamiliar attack recovery. Save broad loadout experiments for after you can read the encounter.

steps.title: Build the resource loop
steps.text: Connect a melee sequence to an ability opportunity rather than treating every button as an isolated damage source. Use the combat guide for the confirmed system relationships.

steps.title: Tune only the pressure you want to change
steps.text: Consider dodge timing for timing difficulty or projectile speed for ranged readability. Pick settings for comfort; there is no requirement to copy another player's configuration.

sections.title: Is it fair to call it a Soulslike?
paragraphs: A genre comparison does not tell you enough about the controls. Melee combat alone does not establish parries, stamina rules, death penalties or a particular boss difficulty. For a purchase decision, compare the confirmed mechanics you care about rather than treating a genre label as a feature list.

sections.title: Identify behavior before choosing a counter

subsections.title: Separate ranged pressure from environmental hazards
paragraphs: An enemy attack and an unsafe floor can look equally urgent but require different responses. Note what is causing damage before assigning a weakness to the nearest target.

subsections.title: Check the in-game name before extending the Wiki
paragraphs: A silhouette is useful for recognition but not enough to name a new species. Record the exact label, location and behavior together so two descriptions of the same enemy do not become duplicate records.

subsections.title: Do not transfer the original game's numbers
paragraphs: A returning family does not guarantee identical damage, health, resistances or spawn behavior. The sequel's melee-focused combat changes the context in which those enemies are fought.

sections.title: Why bosses have their own index
paragraphs: A boss guide needs an encounter location, readable attack patterns and verified rewards. The Central Resonant has a named preview; other pictured entities may still lack a confirmed label. Those cases should not be presented as equally complete records.
